title: Four Forces? Free-Body Diagram Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Aarav drags a box of books down the college corridor with a rope, and it speeds up. How many forces act on the box? Most people say one, his pull. The real answer is four. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we learn to draw a free-body diagram: one body, cut free, with every force that acts on it.

On a live motion notebook a two kilogram block on a rough floor gets its forces one at a time: weight, normal force, tension and friction, with a live readout and an acceleration vs rope pull graph whose slope is one over the mass. A slow-mo replay checks every arrow, and a snapped rope shows there is no "force of motion". Then the five-step method (sum of F = ma along each axis), the giver test link by link, forces on vs forces by side by side, two pause-and-think questions, a worked example on lifting a box, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 How many forces on one box?
0:27 What a free-body diagram is
0:46 Motion notebook: four forces, one at a time
1:39 Slow-mo replay and the snapped rope
2:07 The method in five steps
2:47 Every force needs a giver, link by link
3:05 Forces on vs forces by + pause and think
3:38 Worked example: lifting a box
4:06 Exam trap: only forces on the body
4:25 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:16 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Equilibrium of Forces. Aarav pulls his rope tight, but it always sags. Why?
